newsitem.title: USA: U.S. EPA issues final "credible evidence" rule.
newsitem.headline: U.S. EPA issues final "credible evidence" rule.

text.p: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Tuesday said it issued a final rule to clarify its authority under the Clean Air Act to allow various credible data to be used as evidence on whether a facility is violating emissions standards.
The rule clarifies that information such as continuous emissions monitoring data, engineering analyses, witness testimony and other information can be used to gauge compliance.
The EPA has relied on specific procedures for measuring emissions from industry stacks to determine compliance, but said it had authority to use other information as well.
"The rule does not alter current emissions standards, create any new monitoring or reporting requirements or change the compliance obligations for industry," the EPA said in a statement.
Some industry groups have objected to the rule, saying it would enable the EPA to change the rules for compliance.
